title: ping, traceroute, mtr, nslookup, iperf and bandwidth tests

videos.script: Five tools, and each one answers a single question. {{five}} ping asks whether an address answers, and how long the round trip takes. traceroute asks which routers are on the way. {{ping}} mtr asks the same thing again and again, and counts what goes missing at each hop. nslookup asks a DNS server for a name. iperf3 asks how much a path can carry. {{tools}} Most mistakes with them come from reading an answer to a question the tool never asked. A ping says nothing about a web server. A star in traceroute does not mean a router is broken. {{misread}} In this lesson you will see both. A router that loses eighty per cent of its answers while every packet through it arrives. And a loss rate of twenty per cent that one run reports as twelve. {{loss}} Then you will measure a link shaped to twenty megabits. Upload stays at twenty. Download runs at more than three gigabits, because nobody shaped that direction. {{iperf}} By the end, each number these tools print should tell you what it measured, and what it did not. {{end}}
